texts: good. the identity lands as a clean kind-level claim (the new-moon spring tide is a harvest tide) with both compound terms typed; the only thing not carried is the reverse direction, so a query starting from "the harvest tide" will not come back to the new-moon spring tide.

bad: three things go wrong at once. "Salt-bloom" is a mass noun with no article, so the translator cannot pick out the portion that was harvested and carry it into "that salt-bloom"; nothing in the result clause names the harvest occasion, so the potency floats free of the harvest that produced it; and "for the season" gives no number, so the translator invented a duration of exactly 1. Rewrite as: "Whenever a Keeper harvests a batch of salt-bloom at the new-moon spring tide, that batch stays potent for one season after the harvest." A countable "batch" can be tracked from the condition into the result, "after the harvest" ties the potency to the occasion that caused it, and "one season" states the extent instead of leaving it to be guessed.

good. the reviewer's one objection — that "as a calendar marker" hangs on the tide rather than on the observing — was overruled on adjudication; the observing, the tide, and the marker role are all carried.

good. the restriction "from the full-moon tide" is kept as a condition of a fireable rule, and the change into chalky residue comes out complete (the turning, the resulting state, and the residue property).
good. "cannot explain" becomes one denied-ability bundle, with the moon-phase rule's own typing kept outside the denial so the rule still exists and only the explaining is denied.
good. both predicates land as separate properties of the one pattern.
